summary: GRASP-A2 exhibits geometric collapse and property decodability loss at Layer 12, distinct from random initialization.

claims.claim: A2 undergoes significant representation space contraction at Layer 12 compared to the peak expansion at Layer 8.
claims.evidence: PR drops from 216.8 (L8) to 21.9 (L12); Anisotropy increases from 0.37 to 0.66.
claims.test: RDKit SMARTS: `*` on all atoms; Label column: layer_index=12 vs 8. Prediction: PR variance fraction should drop significantly at L12 for trained models but remain flat (~10) for random weights.

claims.claim: Continuous physicochemical properties (Crippen logp contribution) lose linear decodability at Layer 12.
claims.evidence: Linear R² drops from 0.863 (L4) to 0.633 (L12); MLP R² drops from 0.962 to 0.722.
claims.test: RDKit SMARTS: `[C]` with `df.crippen_logp_contrib`. Prediction: Correlation between atom embedding and Crippen value should decrease at L12 compared to L4 for trained A2, but remain stable (~0.8) for random weights.

claims.claim: Discrete topological features (Ring size, Heteroatom neighbors) survive Layer 12 collapse better than continuous properties.
claims.evidence: Ring5 Linear R² remains 0.927 at L12 vs 0.988 at L4; O-Neighbor MLP stays >0.943.
claims.test: RDKit SMARTS: `[r5]` for Ring5, `[#6]-[O]` for O-neighbor on C. Prediction: Classification accuracy for these discrete labels should remain high (>0.9) at L12 even if continuous regression R² drops.

claims.claim: The collapse is a learned dynamic, not an architectural artifact of depth alone.
claims.evidence: A2_PR(L8)=216.8 -> L12=21.9; A2_Random_PR stays ~10-11 across all layers (L4=10.2, L12=11.2).
claims.test: Compare trained vs random PR trajectories over 50 epochs or layer indices. Prediction: Trained models show non-monotonic PR evolution; Random weights maintain constant low-dimensional noise structure.
claims.prediction: Random model should not exhibit the L8->L12 drop seen in A2.

trivial_explanations: The high anisotropy (0.657) at Layer 12 may reflect standard deep-layer saturation where embeddings align with dominant global features rather than local chemistry.
Crippen R² decline could be due to the MLP probe overfitting earlier layers; however, Linear drop confirms signal loss.
